prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: telling the society a policyholder has died. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a policyholder has died, treat the case as a change in authority first and a claim issue second, because we need to know who can legally speak and act for the estate before any settlement discussion."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the caller mentions a death, I should ask for the date of death and whether a death certificate or solicitor/executor details are available, as those facts shape what we can and cannot do next."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there is a joint policy or another named person on the account, I prefer to confirm whether they are taking over day-to-day contact, because that often lets me keep the claim moving without unnecessary delay."},{"type":"observation","content":"When bereavement is recent, I slow the conversation down and keep my questions short, because people often struggle to take in instructions and can miss important steps if I rush."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the deceased was the main driver or main contact on a motor policy, I need to check immediately who now has the vehicle, where it is kept, and whether it is still insured for use, because cover can be affected by those changes."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the estate is not ready to deal with the claim, I prefer to place the matter on hold with a clear diary note rather than close it, so we can pick it up again when the executor or next of kin is ready."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a bereavement is linked to a loss event, it helps to separate sympathy from liability handling, because the claim may still need standard evidence and triage even though the policyholder cannot assist."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the person reporting the death is not the executor or policy authority, I should avoid giving detailed policy decisions and instead explain that we need confirmation of their right to act for the estate."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a claim is likely to continue under an estate or surviving joint holder, I prefer to summarise the next steps in plain language at the end of the call, because that reduces repeat calls and confusion."},{"type":"observation","content":"When there is any sign of vulnerability or distress, I should offer to repeat information, signpost bereavement support, and record that the contact may need a gentler follow-up, because good triage is as much about care as it is about control of risk."}]}
